hunt.justification: Local privilege escalation is the critical pivot in Linux intrusions. Identifying the outcome (root transition) and precursors (writable paths) provides a durable defense against novel exploit implementations that bypass name-based rules.

meta.name: Linux LPE via Writable Path Execution

related.reason: Focuses on the SUID helpers themselves rather than the path of execution.

meta.analysis: A simple rule might alert on any root process in /tmp, but this hunt uses fleet-wide prevalence to filter noise, scopes via known vulnerabilities, and uses an agent to weigh the entire lifecycle (path + root + discovery).

stages.name: Exploitation of SUID Helpers or Kernel Interfaces

scenario.summary: Exploit binaries are executed from writable Linux directories like /tmp or /dev/shm to trigger kernel memory bugs or abuse SUID-root helpers. This results in a privilege transition where an unprivileged process lineage gains root access, often followed by diagnostic commands like whoami.

meta.rationale: Start with Linux servers hosting public-facing applications or those with known kernel vulnerabilities (CVEs) as identified in the scoping step.
meta.hypothesis: An attacker has achieved root privileges on a Linux host by executing an exploit from a world-writable directory, followed by a transition of the process lineage to UID 0.

hunt.name: Linux LPE via Writable Path Execution
hunt.description: Local privilege escalation (LPE) in Linux often involves a predictable lifecycle: a binary is dropped into a world-writable directory like /tmp or /dev/shm, executed, and leverages a kernel vulnerability or SUID helper to gain root status. This hunt identifies this transition by monitoring processes launched from suspicious paths that eventually run as root, baselining their prevalence across the fleet to identify unique exploit payloads, and corroborating these with post-escalation discovery commands like whoami.

nodes.label: Root processes launched from writable paths

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_path, process_cmd_line, user_name, parent_process_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE user_name = 'root' AND (process_path LIKE '/tmp/%' OR process_path LIKE '/var/tmp/%' OR process_path LIKE '/dev/shm/%' OR process_path LIKE '/run/user/%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify processes running as root whose image resides in world-writable directories, a core indicator of LPE.
config.expected_signal: A row indicates a process that achieved root privileges while running from a directory normally restricted for system binaries.

primitive_config.expected: A row indicates a process that achieved root privileges while running from a directory normally restricted for system binaries.

config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_path) AS full_path, LOWER(process_name) AS proc_name, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (process_path LIKE '/tmp/%' OR process_path LIKE '/dev/shm/%' OR process_path LIKE '/var/tmp/%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY full_path, proc_name HAVING hosts <= 3 ORDER BY hosts ASC
config.description: Identify one-off exploit payloads by baselining the prevalence of all binaries executing from world-writable paths.
config.expected_signal: Unique or rare paths/binaries in /tmp or /dev/shm. Routine scripts appear on many hosts; exploits are typically rare.

primitive_config.label: Rare binaries in writable paths
primitive_config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_path) AS full_path, LOWER(process_name) AS proc_name, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (process_path LIKE '/tmp/%' OR process_path LIKE '/dev/shm/%' OR process_path LIKE '/var/tmp/%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY full_path, proc_name HAVING hosts <= 3 ORDER BY hosts ASC
primitive_config.expected: Unique or rare paths/binaries in /tmp or /dev/shm. Routine scripts appear on many hosts; exploits are typically rare.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_path, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE user_name = 'root' AND instr(',' || '{{discovery_tools}}' || ',', ',' || REPLACE(REPLACE(LOWER(process_name), '/usr/bin/', ''), '/bin/', '') || ',') > 0 AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Find root-owned discovery processes to corroborate that a privilege transition was successful and followed by verification.
config.expected_signal: A 'whoami' or 'id' command running as root. This is the 'finishing move' that confirms the exploit worked.
